134: [edit] On the Ten Days of Repentance, we say "the holy King" and "the King of Justice." If one erred or has doubt [about having said the correct formulation], with respect to "the Holy King" they return to the beginning [of the Amidah], and with respect to "the King of Justice," if they realize their error before moving their feet [at the end of the Amidah], they return to the blessing "Restore..." and continue from there, but if they do not realize until after moving their feet (see chapter 117), they return to the beginning (see chapter 118).
[edit] If one said "the holy God" and then almost immediately realized and said "the holy King]], they do not need to repeat. The same is true for "the King of Justice."

[edit] On Shabbat evening prayers during the Birkat Me'ein Sheva, we say "the Holy King." Rem"a: This is also true when Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbat. The end of the blessing mentions only Shabbat. The same is true when Yom Kippur falls on Shabbat (Mahari"l and Minhagim).
[edit] Some have the practice of praying on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur bent over. These people need to straighten up at the end of each blessing.

[edit] If one did not say "remember us" or "who is like You," they need not repeat. Rem"a: This is the case even if they have not moved their feet [at the end of the Amidah] and have simply finished that blessing [that contains the addition] (Terumat Hadeshen). The same rule applies to somebody who did not say "write..." and "in the book of..." (Tur).
[edit] In the Amidah, one says "You gave us this Day of Judgment" and does not mention that it is Rosh Hodesh.
[edit] If [Rosh Hashanah] falls on a weekday, one says "a day of blasting, a sacred occasion", and if it falls on Shabbat, one says "a remembrance of blasting."

[edit] We do not say "holidays for joy, pilgrimages and times for happiness" and we do not say "and grant for us...". During Mussaf, we do not say "we are unable to ascend and be seen before You." Instead, we say "we are unable to perform our obligations for You," (and we conclude the blessing with "Your word is truth etc." (Tur)).

[edit] Even though during the rest of the year we pray silently, on Rosh Hashanah we have the practice to play out loud. There is no concern about getting lost because everybody has a Machzor. Rem"a: It is the practice that everybody says to their fellow "May you be inscribed for a good year" (Tur).
